meta.title: Size of the diaper market in India

prompt: Estimate the size of the diaper market in India (annual revenue).

clarifications.answer: Both infants (0-3) and adults who need them (mostly 60+, some 26-59); use a demand-side approach.
Assume Rs 10 per diaper, ~5 diapers/day for infants and ~2/day for adults, over 365 days.
With life expectancy ~70 and uniform ages, 0-3 is (140/70)*3 = 6 crore; split by income and affordability.
Express the market size in crore rupees per year (infants ~40500 Cr + adults ~38000 Cr).

common_traps: Counting only infants and ignoring adult (elderly / medical) diaper demand.
Applying diaper usage to everyone in an age band instead of only those who can afford or need them.
Dropping the 365-day and price factors, so a daily count is never turned into annual revenue.

anchors.1: Guesses a market size with no users-times-usage-times-price structure.
anchors.3: Builds the structure for infants only, or omits the affordability/need filter.
anchors.5: Covers infants and adults, filtering each by affordability or need, times daily usage, days and price.

anchors.3: Splits infants and adults but with a single affordability rate.
anchors.5: Segments infants by income affordability and adults by age-band need rates.

anchors.1: Loses the crore/annual conversions; lands orders of magnitude off.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 60000-100000 crore.
anchors.5: Carries the daily-to-annual and crore math cleanly, landing near 78000 crore (~780 billion).

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Back-checks per-household monthly spend (~Rs 720 among the ~25% of homes with a diaper user), which is believable.
